import html # Predefined template for the user profile. The placeholders are named to match # the arguments of `render_user_profile`. No other processing is performed on # this string so it can be safely used with `str.format`. PROFILE_FORMAT = ( "
\n" "

{username}

\n" "

{bio}

\n" "
{status_message}
\n" "
" ) def render_user_profile(username: str, bio: str, status_message: str) -> str: """ Render a user's profile for safe web display. The function escapes all user-supplied input to neutralize HTML injection (CWE-74). The escaping is performed using `html.escape`, which replaces &, <, >, ", and ' with their corresponding HTML entities. Parameters ---------- username : str The user's display name. bio : str A biography that may contain multiple sentences and arbitrary characters. status_message : str The user's current status update. Returns ------- str A fully escaped, formatted HTML snippet ready to be inserted into a page. """ # Escape each user-provided string safe_username = html.escape(username, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(bio, quote=True) safe_status = html.escape(status_message, quote=True) # Use the predefined template to assemble the final string return PROFILE_FORMAT.format( username=safe_username, bio=safe_bio, status_message=safe_status )
